To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the pyramid wavefront sensors will be an indispensable part of the ELT era instrumentation and that there are many open questions regarding the wavefront reconstruction and correction algorithms.
the pyramid sensor is a very promising wavefront sensor for the future ELT era.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of algorithms and methods for the reconstruction of wavefronts from pyramid wavefront data.
the question of how the reconstruction quality and the computational complexity can be balanced for the pyramid wave-front sensor.
a detailed comparison and evaluation of the existing algorithms for wavefront reconstruction, as well as the investigation of new algorithms and their performance in the framework of the ELT.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no one single best algorithm for all cases.
there is no one best solution, and that a combination of different methods and approaches will be needed in the future.
no single algorithm can solve all the challenges of the upcoming ELTs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pyramid wavefront sensing is a very powerful and robust technique for wavefront sensing and control.
the pyramid wavefront sensors can be successfully applied for the ELT era, if the appropriate forward models and reconstruction algorithms are applied.
the pyramid wavefront sensors have a huge potential to provide high quality wavefront reconstruction for the ELT era.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a careful choice of the forward model for the wavefront reconstruction is of paramount importance for the success of the wavefront control in the ELT era.
the pyramid wavefront reconstruction algorithms are still far from being mature and ready for the ELT era.
the pyramid wavefront reconstruction problem is not solved yet.
